name: ADAR-Mediated Site-Directed RNA Editing (SDRE)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Correct pathogenic RNA sequences by recruiting endogenous ADAR enzymes to catalyze adenosine-to-inosine (A→I) editing without altering genomic DNA.
molecularDefect: Pathogenic variants that can be functionally corrected through A→I (interpreted as G) RNA editing.
diseaseMechanism: A chemically modified antisense guide RNA hybridizes with the target transcript, forming a duplex that recruits endogenous ADAR. ADAR deaminates a specific adenosine to inosine, restoring correct RNA sequence or protein function.
suitableVariantTypes: G>A pathogenic variants (or mutations correctable by A→I editing); selected nonsense and missense mutations where editing restores protein function.
typicalDiseases: Hurler syndrome (proof-of-concept); inherited retinal diseases; neurological disorders; additional monogenic diseases under preclinical investigation.
rnaTargetRegion: Target adenosine within pre-mRNA or mature mRNA that is accessible for guide-RNA binding and ADAR recruitment.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript must contain an editable adenosine and permit formation of a suitable ADAR-recognition duplex.
asoChemistry: Chemically modified ADAR-recruiting antisense oligonucleotides (e.g., phosphorothioate, 2′-OMe, LNA-containing guide oligonucleotides depending on platform).
typicalLength: Approximately 20–30 nucleotides, depending on guide design and ADAR recruitment strategy.
designRules: Literature synthesis: create a stable RNA duplex; position the editable adenosine opposite the designed mismatch; optimize ADAR recruitment while minimizing bystander editing; experimentally confirm editing efficiency by RNA sequencing.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Target region should be accessible for guide-RNA hybridization and formation of an ADAR-compatible double-stranded RNA substrate.
offTargetConsiderations: Bystander A→I editing within the guide-RNA duplex; unintended editing at partially complementary transcripts; transcriptome-wide RNA editing analysis is recommended.
advantages: Reversible; no permanent DNA modification; exploits endogenous ADAR enzymes; enables correction of selected pathogenic variants at the RNA level.
limitations: Restricted to editable adenosines; editing efficiency varies among tissues and targets; potential bystander editing; no approved therapeutic yet.
clinicalTrialExamples: Preclinical and early translational ADAR-editing platforms (e.g., RESTORE, LEAPER, CLUSTER); no late-stage approved clinical program yet. (Nature)

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic and preclinical evidence; clinical translation is ongoing.

referencesSummary: Qu et al. (2019); Merkle et al. (2019); Bertoli et al. (2025); Fisher (2024).
